candidates.rationale: A week-long volatility burst is inventory risk being priced in a profitable firm (it reverts) but genuine bad news in an unprofitable one (it drifts), so profitability tells you which vol expansions to fade.

The best and worst day of the past fortnight net out to the direction of the largest liquidity shock, and measured in units of the stock's own normal volatility that shock is the premium paid to whoever absorbed it, which is repaid as the price snaps back.

Days elapsed since the biggest absolute move separates drift built by gradual information diffusion, which continues, from drift manufactured by one recent jump, which reverses; the month's risk-adjusted drift is only worth following in the first case.
Sessions that travel further above the open than below it reveal large orders being worked one-sided through the day, and the unfilled remainder of that demand keeps pressing prices for weeks.

Half-year drift and two-week overreaction are opposite-signed and come from different investors (slow institutional rebalancing versus dealer inventory), so the spread buys long-trending names that just pulled back rather than paying up for extended ones.

Institutions split large orders across many days, so a profitable firm that rose on most days rather than on a few big ones is being accumulated, and the residual order flow keeps arriving after the signal is observed.

Profitability that improved over two reported quarters while the stock sits at the bottom of its own two-week price distribution is a fundamental turn the tape has not taken in yet, and the gap closes as estimates are revised.

When most of a month's movement lands in a single day the move was an event rather than gradual repricing, and for accrual-heavy firms such earnings-day repricings keep going because more reversal of accruals is coming, while in clean-accrual names the same concentration is a liquidity event that reverts.

Weighting the month's returns toward the most recent days measures how much of the move is still fresh and un-intermediated; in units of normal volatility a large fresh move is inventory that dealers must still lay off, so it reverses, while an older move of the same size has already been absorbed.

A trend accompanied by a quarter of rising realised volatility is a crowded, leverage-financed move that unwinds when risk budgets bind, whereas the same trend under stable or falling volatility is orderly repricing that continues.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Retuning one constant or one price field of an archived expression is not novelty: EMA 42 for EMA 10, range window 63 for 21, and $high for $close inside TS_MAX were all caught as subtree overlap or rho >= 0.91.
  2. Changing the normalizer under an unchanged numerator gave rho 0.996 (TS_STD versus TS_SUM(ABS) over TS_SUM($return, 63)); novelty has to come from the numerator's field or sign structure, not the denominator.
  3. The stochastic / range-position template ($close against TS_MIN and TS_MAX of the same window) lost three proposals this round to duplicate and correlation; stop sampling that shape here.
  4. Fitness clustered at 1.97 to 3.64 where two widely separated windows were ratioed or two CS_RANKs of different signal families were multiplied; single-window distance-from-high and IF-gated regime switches scored ~0.42 and are already covered.
  5. $operating_margin and $asset_turnover caused both coverage failures (0.853, 0.893) plus three cheap-screen misses at |t| 0.13-0.52; retire both fields. The fundamentals that carried every accepted leg were $roe, $roa, $accrual_gap and TS_DELTA($leverage, 63).
  6. Combine a fundamental leg and a price/volume leg by subtracting two cross-sectional ranks; every fitness above 3.0 had that shape, while products of two CS_ZSCORE legs were the single largest cheap-screen failure group (5 of 8).
  7. Stop using TS_SUM($return, n) over 21-105 days as a standalone leg: three such proposals screened at |t| 0.37-0.50, and the one accepted 5-day version scored 0.030.
  8. In price_volume niches, short/long moving-average ratios of $close, $high, $low topped out near fitness 1.0; the only strong one (2.835) used TS_ARGMIN/TS_ARGMAX position over a 189-day window. Prefer long-window timing/position operators over MA ratios there.
  9. Shift proposal budget toward mixed niches: they returned 3.14-5.04 this round versus 0.03-2.84 for pure price_volume, across all three speeds.
  10. Swapping only the outer wrapper (CS_RANK to CS_DEMEAN or CS_ZSCORE) or replacing one leaf with its TS_MEAN over a new window is not novelty; all five archive_subtree rejections were exactly that, sharing 5-12 nodes. Change the operator skeleton or the data fields instead.
  11. Three mutations landed 4-8 edits away because a fresh short expression was attached to an unrelated parent. Either pick a parent that already shares the skeleton and change one window or one field, or submit the idea as a new seed rather than a mutation.
  12. Track proposals already made this run before submitting bare single-fundamental ranks: both duplicates were canonical one-liners over $roa and $roe.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
Leave `parent_ids` empty and `changed_node` empty for EXPLORE.
